clue.text: It's fated, all the time children will ask 'are we nearly there yet?'

definitions.meaning: the doctrine or state of being fated in advance

definitions.text: all the time children will ask 'are we nearly there yet?'
definitions.meaning: read as ..., the whole stretch of a journey before reaching the destination, when children pester

explanation.surface: A weary parent reflects that the back-seat chorus of 'are we nearly there yet?' is simply their destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as PRE + DESTINATION: the time before you arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Predestination is the belief that events are settled beforehand, so whatever happens was fated.

clue.text: For neuralgia, I dropped ecstasy — it's a gas

parts.note: PRO means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the I is dropped from the pain word

parts.note: neuralgia is nerve PAIN
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that to treat nerve pain they took ecstasy, which is a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a gas' reads as 'it's great fun'; 'gas' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a hydrocarbon fuel gas used in cylinders for heating and cooking.

clue.text: E-reader in US state supporting English lit

indicators.note: in a down answer the following letters support, sitting beneath, the English letter
the e-reader is placed in the state's letters

parts.note: ND is North Dakota
the KINDLE is Amazon's e-reader

explanation.surface: An e-reader propping up English literature in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit' looks like literature; it is the past tense of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To enkindle is to set alight, so enkindled means set on fire.

clue.text: Media boss longing to get spinning

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newspaper boss
DYING means longing, as in 'dying to see you'

explanation.surface: A media executive is keen to give a story some spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddying water whirls in circles, so it is swirling round and round.

clue.text: Sleep after sex, getting up before end of day in confused state

indicators.note: the sleep letters come after the reversed sex word
the earlier pieces come before the last letter
in a down answer getting up reads the letters upwards, reversing them

parts.note: IT is slang for sex
ZZ represents snoring sleep, as in comics

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A bedroom scene: sleep after sex, rising before day ends, all in a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'getting up' reads upwards, giving TI; IT for sex is a long-standing crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A tizzy is a state of nervous agitation, a flap.

clue.text: Endless money and gold is melted down for coinage

indicators.note: melting down metal destroys its form, so the letters are recast in a new order
endless removes the last letter from each of money and gold

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Cash and bullion are smelted to make new coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MONEY to MONE and GOLD to GOL; with IS they are rearranged by 'melted down'. 'coinage' means a newly coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word, a coinage in the sense of creating language.

clue.text: Revolutionary trading extremes for religion

indicators.note: the first and last letters trade places, swapping the word's ends

parts.note: a MAOIST is a follower of the revolutionary Mao Zedong

explanation.surface: A revolutionary swaps radical positions in exchange for faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading extremes' swaps the M and T at the ends of MAOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is a Chinese religious and philosophical tradition based on the Tao, the way.

clue.text: Skin of cattle in East End compound

parts.note: OX is a bovine animal, cattle

indicators.note: London's East End cockney accent drops the H sound

parts.note: HIDE is an animal skin

explanation.surface: Cowhide on sale in a London East End enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the cockney part of London, where speakers drop their Hs. 'compound' is a chemical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: Rest, stirring before morning run

indicators.note: the mixed letters come before the morning abbreviation
stirring mixes the letters of rest into a new order

explanation.surface: After a lie-in, someone wakes before breakfast and goes for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like waking up; it rearranges REST as STRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a small river, and a run is a dialect word for a brook.

clue.text: Multi-volume work about a king kept in wood

indicators.note: the work goes round, or about, the other letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: OED, the Oxford English Dictionary, runs to many volumes
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A many-volumed history book discusses a monarch held captive in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept in wood' sounds like imprisonment in a forest; it describes wine or spirit matured in oak barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaked wine has been aged in oak casks, so it has been stored in timber.

clue.text: Connoisseur of beastly habits squeezed zits outside flipping work toilet!

indicators.note: the squeezed spots end up on the outside, wrapping round the next letters
squeezing pushes the spots' letters out of shape into a new order
flipping turns the word pair over so it is read backwards

parts.note: GO means work, as in 'the engine won't go'
LOO is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: A disgusted observer at the office reports someone popping spots in the work loo, a beastly habit indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezed' gives Z...IST; 'flipping' gives OOLOG. 'Beastly habits' means the habits of beasts, not nasty behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoologist studies animals, so is an expert on the ways of beasts.

clue.text: Regular payment some native Americans, lacking capital, received

indicators.note: the word for some takes in, or receives, the other piece inside it

parts.note: ANY means some, as in 'have you got any?'

indicators.note: capital here is the first letter, which the people's name must lose

parts.note: the Inuit are indigenous peoples of the Arctic regions of North America

explanation.surface: Some indigenous Americans, without funds, were given an allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking capital' looks financial, but capital here means a first letter; it leaves NUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed sum paid every year, a regular income such as a pension.

clue.text: Dramatic incident following live programme that's indecent

indicators.note: the incident comes after, or follows, the programme in the answer

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast, a programme transmitted live from a location
a SCENE is a dramatic outburst or incident

explanation.surface: A shocking moment on live TV is condemned as lewd.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to accepted standards of decency, so it is a stronger synonym of indecent.

clue.text: Singing praises of bloc's singular handling of operations

parts.note: EU, the European Union, is a trading bloc
logistics is the handling of operations; made singular it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone praises the EU for its unique management of activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' seems to mean remarkable, but it asks for LOGISTICS without its plural S.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of praise, so eulogistic language is full of acclaim.

clue.text: Magazine laid out in Pret and Costa

indicators.note: laying out the letters arranges them in a new order

explanation.surface: A periodical is displayed in high-street sandwich and coffee chains.
explanation.walkthrough: Pret A Manger and Costa Coffee are British high-street café chains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly political magazine.

clue.text: Fancy that man pursuing women

indicators.note: the man comes after the women, chasing them, in the answer

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on clothing labels or toilet doors
HIM is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A gossip exclaims at the sight of some fellow chasing women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that' reads as an exclamation, but 'Fancy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is a passing whim or impulse of desire.

clue.text: Edit out first husband — it's helpful to groom

indicators.note: the husband letter comes first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to AIRBRUSH a photo is to edit out blemishes

explanation.surface: A wedding photo retoucher removes the bride's former husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' suggests a bridegroom; it is a verb, to tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairbrush is a tool for tidying hair, so it aids grooming.

clue.text: Football bosses note Portuguese performance

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, governs English football
DO is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Football administrators observe a show in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a verb meaning observe; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Fado is a melancholy Portuguese song style, performed in Lisbon's bars.

clue.text: Look out for the ball! Are you caught up in excitement?

indicators.note: the golfer's warning catches, or holds, the next letters inside

parts.note: FORE is the warning cry shouted by golfers

indicators.note: in a down answer up reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: R U is text-speak for are you

explanation.surface: A golfer's warning cry and a question to someone hit in the commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'up' reverses, giving UR; RU as text-speak for 'are you' is a modern convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is an outburst of public excitement or anger, an uproar.

clue.text: Allowing leeway in how courier might be paid?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a fee for each letter delivered

explanation.surface: A query about the latitude given in a courier's pay arrangements.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as PER MISSIVE: a messenger paid for each letter carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A permissive regime is lax, granting people latitude to do as they like.

clue.text: Boom and bust leaving business with an austerity champion

parts.note: a boom is a SPAR on a ship, holding the sail

indicators.note: the business abbreviation leaves the word bust, taken out of it

explanation.surface: A tale of economic cycles: an austerity hawk comments on boom and bust in business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boom and bust' looks economic; boom is a ship's spar. 'leaving' removes BUS from BUST to leave T.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan, like the ancient Spartans, embraces frugal, severe living.

clue.text: I'll dismiss judge in case of ecocide — court in uproar after union's barred

indicators.note: the judge's letter goes in the outer pair
the case of a word is its outer letters
uproar throws the court's letters into disorder
barred means shut out, so the union's letter is removed

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for union

explanation.surface: A judge in an ecocide trial threatens to dismiss the case as the court erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barred' leaves CORT and 'in uproar' scrambles it to CTOR. The definition is the device speaking for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector throws people or things out, so it could say of itself that it expels.

clue.text: Ahead, having broken Djokovic? Fantastic!

indicators.note: the ahead word breaks into the player, splitting it

parts.note: Novak Djokovic, the tennis champion, is a SERB
UP means ahead, as in 'two sets up'

explanation.surface: A tennis fan cheers having broken Djokovic's serve to go in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' suggests breaking serve in tennis; here UP breaks into SERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb is an exclamation of delight, a near synonym for excellent.

clue.text: Regret engaging a left-leaning barrister, taking time to find what's needed for court battle

indicators.note: the regret word engages, or holds, the next letters within it

parts.note: RUE means regret

indicators.note: leaning to the left, in an across answer, reads the letters backwards

parts.note: a QC is a Queen's Counsel, a senior barrister

explanation.surface: A litigant rues hiring a leftish lawyer and needing time to prepare for a court fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis or squash court, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: A racquet is the bat used in tennis or squash, so a player needs one to compete on court.

clue.text: Carp droppings picked up by SA rodent

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the phrase is matched by sound

parts.note: a KOI is an ornamental carp, and POO means droppings

explanation.surface: A South American rodent scavenges fish droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: British walk (one way or another) to pick fruit

parts.note: a RAMBLE is a leisurely country walk

explanation.surface: A British hiker strolls along, gathering fruit on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: '(one way or another)' notes the parse also works as BR + AMBLE; it is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bramble is to go gathering blackberries, the fruit of the bramble bush.

clue.text: Georgia's brother picking up a streaker?

indicators.note: the brother picks up, gathering in, the next letter

parts.note: BRER is a Southern US dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit from Georgia folk tales

explanation.surface: A southern US man's brother collects someone running naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Brer Rabbit stories come from Georgia. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked in public, so is one who bares more than others: a barer.

clue.text: Poet, republican, reinterpreted myths about eastern queen

indicators.note: the reworked myths go about, or around, the next letter
reinterpreting the myths rearranges their letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A republican poet retells myths about an oriental queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reinterpreted' rearranges MYTHS as HYMST, which goes 'about' E to make HYMEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of verses, often a slightly dismissive word for a poet.

clue.text: Take the mickey out of tense relative

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
an AUNT is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone teases a nervous family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the mickey out of' is British slang for mock or tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to jeer at or mock someone, the same as ridiculing them.

clue.text: Say opium eater is a calculating type

parts.note: opium is an example of something that numbs, a NUMBER
a CRUNCHER is something that crunches food, an eater

explanation.surface: An opium addict is called a scheming character.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not as a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A number cruncher is someone who does complicated sums, such as an accountant.
